note: Exact counters measured against the synthetic fixture in internal/perfbench. These are integers, not timings: identical on every machine, unaffected by ambient load. internal/perfbench/counters_test.go fails when one grows (a regression) and also when one shrinks (an unrecorded gain). Wall clock is never gated here; see the benchmarks for why.

targets.sourceParsesPerReleaseWithThreeViruses: Reached: 4, one parse per source file, down from 12. GoSourceFile.Incubate now takes the whole mutator set and parses once for all of them. With the default 14 mutators this is 14 parses per file reduced to 1.
targets.astWalksPerReleaseWithThreeViruses: 12 is correct and must not grow. Each mutator needs its own pass over the tree, so this scales with the mutator count by design. It is recorded separately from parses because the two were the same number until the parse was shared, which is what let an earlier counter claim to measure parses while only ever measuring walks.
targets.laboratoryRunsPerReleaseWholeFixture: 48 is correct for whole-fixture scope and must not grow. The staged goal is different: a native scope should let a caller ask for the mutants a change justifies and pay only for those. Each run costs one `go test` invocation, measured at 700-1100ms of fixed overhead regardless of how fast the suite itself is.
targets.filesLinkedPerSandbox: 6 working files, down from 11 once the walk stopped descending into .git. This is what ONE sandbox costs; it is no longer paid per mutant, so read it together with sandboxesBuiltPerRelease. Measured at ~0.45ms per file.
targets.sandboxesBuiltPerRelease: Reached 1, down from one per mutant (48 on this fixture). Laboratory pools sandboxes and restores the mutated file before handing one back, so a sequential run builds exactly one and a parallel run builds as many as its peak concurrency. Removal moved to the end of the run, registered through t.Cleanup in Release.
